colour.description: Its flight plan's item 19 A/, its colour and markings

equipment.description: Its flight plan's item 10a, its navigation, communication and approach equipment (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-2)

inspections.description: Its inspections and tests, as recorded, each with the last day it is good for

openSquawks.description: Its squawks not yet fixed, newest first

surveillance.description: Its flight plan's item 10b, its surveillance equipment (AIM Appendix 4, TBL 4-3)

vorCheck.description: Its last VOR check for IFR (14 CFR 91.171): when, how, where, the bearing error, and the last day it is good for -- 30 days on, if the error was within the check's limit

access.description: SIGN_IN: a session can be had, and the developer's workspace needs the role. OPEN: nobody can sign in and everything is open (the local stack). CLOSED: nobody can sign in, and writes and the developer's workspace are refused.

claudeFeatures.description: Where no subscription is sold, who has the features Claude writes: OFF, DEVELOPERS, or EVERYONE signed in.

providers.description: The OIDC providers with real credentials, by registration id: the sign-in buttons to offer. Empty where only the emailed link signs in (the local stack).

subscriptions.description: Whether this deployment sells the subscription; where not, the page says nothing of one.

ChecklistDto.description: An airplane's checklist, as its owner writes it from its flight manual

approachesInWindow.description: Approaches logged in the 6 calendar months before this one

instrumentCurrentUntil.description: The last day of instrument currency (14 CFR 61.57(c)(1), or 61.57(d)'s check); in the past where it has lapsed, null where none is logged

ipcNeededAfter.description: The day after which only an instrument proficiency check restores it (61.57(d))

ipcOn.description: The last instrument proficiency check, as the pilot gives it

trackingInWindow.description: Intercepting and tracking courses logged in them

FeatureUse.description: One paid feature's uses this month (UTC)

FlightPlanFilingRequest.description: A flight plan, FAA Form 7233-4's items

departureTime.description: The departure time, an instant (item 13, UTC)

InspectionsDto.description: An airplane's inspections and tests as recorded, each with the last day it is good for: the annual to the end of the 12th calendar month after (14 CFR 91.409(a)), the altimeter and static test and the transponder test to the end of the 24th (91.411(a), 91.413(a)), the ELT's inspection to the end of the 12th (91.207(d)); the 100-hour due at 100 hours of time in service after the last (91.409(b)). Null where not recorded

eltBatteryDueOn.description: The date the ELT's battery is to be replaced by, as marked on it (91.207(c))

developer.description: Whether this pilot also does development work here: the training workspace and the developer console are theirs, a plain pilot's are not.

email.description: Email address from the identity provider

fullName.description: Their name as their certificate gives it: the pilot in command a flight plan names (item 19 C/) and an endorsement names them by

homeBase.description: Their airplane's home base, an airport identifier

phone.description: Their telephone number, the contact a flight plan's item 19 C/ asks for

SubscriptionDto.description: The signed-in pilot's subscription to the paid features

entitled.description: Whether the paid features are theirs now

plan.description: MONTHLY or YEARLY, when paid for

state.description: FREE (none), TRIAL (the free month), SUBSCRIBED (paid for), or COMPED (given: a developer's, an instructor's)

store.description: Where it was bought, when paid for

trialAvailable.description: Whether the free month is still theirs to start: once an account

until.description: When the free month or the paid time runs out; null for FREE and COMPED

uses.description: This month's uses of each paid feature Claude writes, against its cap

VorCheckDto.description: A VOR check for IFR (14 CFR 91.171)

goodThrough.description: The last day it is good for: 30 days on (91.171(a)(2))

limitDeg.description: The largest error 91.171 allows for this kind of check, degrees

404.description: No iOS app set up here

429.description: Too many codes asked for from here

post.summary: A code for a TV to sign in with

get.description: Sends the browser to the planner, which asks the pilot to confirm with its own sign-in dialog and then POSTs the token. Opening the link uses nothing up, so a mail scanner that fetches it before the pilot does cannot spend their token.

post.description: 302 into the app, now signed in -- a developer to dev mode, anyone else to the planner -- on success; 400 for an expired, already-used or unrecognized token.

post.description: framework=langgraph (nav-log-agent) or framework=crewai (crewai-agent), each a real billed Claude call. The body is the nav log the flight planning drawer shows (departure_ident, destination_ident, aircraft_name, altitude_ft, altitude_selection, legs); the response is newline-delimited JSON: delta lines with text as it is written, then a done line with the whole briefing, or an error line.

delete.description: The pilot and everything that was theirs -- aircraft, flights with their nav logs and tracks, logbook, endorsements, their own checkpoint notes, the sign-in links sent to them -- and every session they hold. Nothing is deleted when the planner cannot take the notes (502).

502.description: Nothing deleted: the planner could not take the notes

get.description: Creates the pilot record on first sign-in. 204, with nothing, when no one is signed in: the ordinary answer for a signed-out page, not a refusal.

put.description: What a flight plan's item 19 C/ asks with the pilot in command's name (AIM Appendix 4), both at once; blank is none. Their name is set with PUT /api/training/name.

put.summary: The signed-in pilot's telephone number and home base
